positions.text: Emergence of a new regulation: informational disclosure modalities in the hedge fund opacity world states that disclosing information previously known only to hedge funds can reduce failures caused by information asymmetry, while distinguishing disclosure forms and microeconomic from macroeconomic consequences. This qualifies Kaal's narrower claim that a public database limited to nonproprietary information may demystify the industry without resolving opacity-driven liquidity risk. The abstract does not show that public nonproprietary disclosure fixes liquidity risk or identify a sufficient disclosure modality.

The abstract does not extend the finding abroad, cover the 2005-to-2015 period specifically, or establish that every venture-capital-backed company causes innovation.

The abstract does not establish that all measured innovation is disruptive or that dollar flows alone identify regulatory need.
